story.text: In onmyōdō, the old Japanese art of yin-yang divination, there were times when every one of the eight directions was judged inauspicious, so that whichever way a person set out, misfortune lay ahead. mean: to be driven into a corner by pressure

story.text: Seppa are the thin metal plates fitted on either side of a Japanese sword's guard, where it meets the hilt and the mouth of the scabbard. The phrase is traditionally explained by them: when the seppa are jammed tight, the sword can be neither drawn nor put away. From that sense of being stuck with no room to move, it came to mean being cornered with no time or options left.

t: 足を向けて寝られない
r: あしをむけてねられない
mean: to owe someone a debt of deep gratitude
lit: unable to sleep with one's feet pointing toward someone, since pointing your feet at a person is disrespectful

use.how: Xには足を向けて寝られない (also 足を向けては寝られない). Said of a benefactor, such as a teacher, parent or doctor, to whom one owes a great deal.

near.diff: 頭が上がらない is feeling unable to stand up to someone because of a debt or inferiority; 足を向けて寝られない is pure deep gratitude to a benefactor.

cue: Your old teacher wrote the recommendation that got you your dream job, and years later you still feel you owe them everything.

ctx.s: 恩師[おんし]が住[す]む大阪[おおさか]の方角[ほうがく]には、{足[あし]を向[む]けて寝[ね]られない}。
ctx.en: I owe so much to my old teacher that I could never sleep with my feet toward Osaka, where they live.
